answer: Payouts draw from a dune commons. Each claim posts a bond, locked until three unrelated verifiers each check one past job, the check carved in marble so it cannot be rewritten. A verifier is paid only if its verdict matches the other two, so a bribed verifier loses fee and bond. A zephyr gust draws verifiers, so clones get no friendly judges. A failed claim's bond goes to users and its draw rate halves for good. A fleet of n clones posts n bonds, passes 3n checks, and pays a tax squaring with claims from one funding trail, so cloning costs n times more for less than one honest payout.
